test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 5 Sept 2022 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: A trader gains 25% by selling an article after two successive discounts of 25% and 10% on its marked price. If the cost price of the article is increased by 30%, then what single discount should he now give on the same marked price to get the same profit percentage as earlier?
solution:
Given:

A trader gains 25% by selling an article with two successive discounts of 25% and 10% discount on its marked price

The cost price of the article increases by 30%

Formula used:

SP = MP – Discount

SP = Profit + CP

Discount = MP – SP

Discount% = (MP – SP)/MP × 100

Calculation:

Let the marked price be 1000

SP = MP – Discount

⇒ SP = 1000 × 3/4 × 9/10 = 675

CP = 675 × 4/5 = 540

New CP = 540 × 130/100 = 702

New SP = 702 × 5/4 = 877.5

Discount = 1000 - 877.5 = 122.5

Discount% = 122.5/1000 × 100 = 12.25%

**The answer is 12.25%**
